title: Approximation and Percentage Error
seo_title: Percentage Error – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Round numbers to decimal places and significant figures; find limits of accuracy; calculate percentage error. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on approximation: significant figures, decimal places, limits of accuracy and percentage error. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The greatest error is half of the unit used.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Count significant figures from the first digit that is not zero.
  • A value correct to the nearest unit can be up to half a unit too big or too small.
  • Percentage error = (error ÷ actual value) × 100%.

Examples

Example

A length of 48 cm is measured as 50 cm

2 ÷ 48 × 100

Answer: 4.17%

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the zeros at the front0.0045 has 2 significant figures.
Dividing by the measured valueDivide by the actual value.
Using the whole unit as the errorThe greatest error is half the unit.

faq.q: What are the limits of 6 cm to the nearest cm?

faq.a: It compares errors of different sizes fairly.

items.q: The length x cm is rounded to the nearest whole number. The result is 32. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: Half of 1 is 0.5. The lower bound is 32 − 0.5 and the upper bound is 32 + 0.5. The upper bound itself would round up, so use <: 31.5 ≤ x < 32.5.

items.q: The mass x g is rounded to the nearest 5. The result is 265. What is the error interval for x?
items.e: Half of 5 is 2.5. The lower bound is 265 − 2.5 and the upper bound is 265 + 2.5. The upper bound itself would round up, so use <: 262.5 ≤ x < 267.5.
